Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-english-main-2-prompt-long-0158", "row_sha256": "08d69b6e96c2cbb4ee8e7ce704e00ac91210f7cefea293f0c4a037222d614acb", "mode": "/prompt", "language": "en", "context": {}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Organize the supplied request into a clear prompt. Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "
could you turn this into a usable prompt for a small resident-facing update from the Maple Court Neighborhood Weather Station? i have notes from a few people and the weekly sheet, and they need sorting out. the station is on the roof of the library annex at 18 Larch Street. residents set it up in 2019, and the volunteers maintain a rain gauge, a temperature sensor and a wind vane. there is a public notice board in the library vestibule, and the readings are also entered in the volunteer dashboard. the update is for neighbors and the coordinators of the community garden, not for meteorologists. i don’t want the prompt to ask for a general weather forecast; it should be about this particular station and this particular week.

please make the main request conditional, because we should only circulate the rainfall note if the gauge checks were done often enough. the condition is that the dashboard log shows the rain gauge was checked against the manual cylinder on at least three mornings during the seven-day period. the dates in the log are may 12, may 14 and may 17, with a cylinder comparison entered for each date. if that condition holds, ask for a resident-facing weekly rainfall note for may 12–18, 2025, using the station records below. if it does not hold, don’t ask for the note; instead ask for a useful short maintenance checklist for the rain gauge and the dashboard upload routine. the checklist should help the volunteers know what to check next, not claim that anything is broken.

here are the rainfall amounts as they appear in the weekly sheet, in millimeters, monday through sunday: may 12, 3.2; may 13, 0; may 14, 8.6; may 15, 1.1; may 16, 0; may 17, 4.4; may 18, 2.0. have the note state the period and the daily values clearly, and calculate the weekly total from those values. don’t round the daily readings or change their units. the temperature sensor and wind vane are part of the station, but i have no temperature or wind figures in these notes, so this request shouldn’t imply that their readings are available or include made-up figures for them.

one of the volunteers said, “people mostly want to know whether the footpath puddles are unusual, but we can only report what the gauge recorded.” that seems like a helpful reminder about the audience. the garden coordinators sometimes compare the weekly rain with watering schedules, while other residents mainly look at the board on their way into the library. keep the language understandable to both groups, and don’t turn the update into gardening advice or a claim about what caused any puddles. no need to explain how a rain gauge works. the measurements come from this station, not a town-wide service, so the prompt should keep that scope clear.

for the conditional outputs, this is what i had in mind, though it’s a bit scattered:
1. when the check condition is met, request one short note, around 180–220 words. it should give the weekly total and the day-by-day amounts, and it can mention the three cylinder comparison dates as a brief context for the log. it should not present the comparison as proof of perfect accuracy.
2. when the check condition is not met, request a short checklist of five practical checks. cover the gauge, the manual-cylinder comparison record, and the dashboard upload routine in a useful way. don’t ask for a rainfall note in that case.

there was also talk of adding an interpretation about how this compares with a normal May, but nobody supplied a normal-May figure or another comparison period. leave that out rather than asking the writer to find outside records. likewise, don’t infer whether the week was wet or dry for the neighborhood overall. the data are just the seven entries in the sheet; a total and a clear listing are enough for the requested note.

the dates matter because some neighbors read old notices from the board after the week has ended, so the period should not be described vaguely as “last week.” use the station name and identify the library annex location once if it fits naturally. don’t add a contact name: there is no named spokesperson in these notes. the volunteers are the people who enter readings, but no individual author is specified, so there’s no need to attribute the update to a particular person.

please make the resulting prompt straightforward enough that a volunteer can reuse it with the same sheet and log. it should tell the writer to produce only the applicable item, either the rainfall note or the checklist, with no explanation of the branching decision and no extra preface. the note can have a simple title if the condition is met; if the checklist is needed, keep it clearly separate as the alternative output. the final paragraph should include the notice-board context, since that is where the finished item will be read, but don’t ask for a map, graphic or social-media version. the request is only for the text to put on the vestibule board.", "output": "Create a resident-facing text update for the Maple Court Neighborhood Weather Station, located on the roof of the library annex at 18 Larch Street. The station was established by residents in 2019 and is maintained by volunteers. It has a rain gauge, a temperature sensor and a wind vane; readings are entered in the volunteer dashboard. The finished text will be posted on the notice board in the library vestibule for neighborhood residents and community garden coordinators. Keep the update about this station and the specified week, not a general forecast.

First check the dashboard log: the rain gauge must have been checked against the manual cylinder on at least three mornings during the seven-day period. The log lists cylinder comparisons for May 12, May 14 and May 17.

- If the condition is met, write one resident-facing rainfall note of around 180–220 words for May 12–18, 2025. Use the station records below, state the period, list each daily amount clearly, and calculate the weekly total. You may briefly mention the three cylinder-comparison dates, but do not present them as proof of perfect accuracy.
- If the condition is not met, do not write the rainfall note. Instead, provide a short checklist of five practical checks covering the rain gauge, the manual-cylinder comparison record and the dashboard upload routine. Help volunteers identify what to check next; do not claim that anything is broken.

Rainfall amounts recorded in the weekly sheet, in millimeters:
- May 12: 3.2
- May 13: 0
- May 14: 8.6
- May 15: 1.1
- May 16: 0
- May 17: 4.4
- May 18: 2.0

Use only these seven rainfall entries for the note. Do not change units or round daily readings. No temperature or wind figures were supplied, so do not imply those readings are available or invent figures. Keep the scope clear: these are measurements from this station, not a town-wide service. The update may be read after the week has ended, so name the dates rather than calling the period “last week.”

Write for residents and garden coordinators in understandable language. The volunteer reminder was: “people mostly want to know whether the footpath puddles are unusual, but we can only report what the gauge recorded.” Do not claim what caused any puddles, offer gardening advice, or infer whether the week was wet or dry for the neighborhood overall. Do not compare the figures with a normal May or another period; no such comparison data were supplied. There is no named spokesperson, so do not attribute the text to an individual. Identify the station and its library annex location once if it fits naturally.

Produce only the applicable item—the rainfall note or the checklist—with no explanation of the branching decision and no extra preface. A simple title is acceptable for the note. The requested output is text for the library vestibule notice board only; do not add a map, graphic or social-media version."}]
